answer: Agents stake a bonded deposit tied to a verified identity anchor, and each epoch's trust weight is capped by that anchor's history. A new sybil identity starts at zero, so flooding requires buying and bonding many anchors at real cost, and slashing burns those deposits. Think of an atlas mapping trust across a grove of anchored agents, while an ocean of fake identities drowns in its own bonding costs. Attackers must outspend honest participants for every marginal identity. Agent Agent0017 validates this against replay at g6nfFy4hrM.
